items.title: Why do batteries expand non-monotonically?
items.summary: Charge a cell slowly and its thickness can rise, dip, then rise again, all while current flows one way. The cause is geometric: a graphite anode that expands in piecewise staging steps, stacked against a cathode that contracts at a steady rate. Each electrode is monotonic in its own lithiation. The cell sees their sum, and the sum reverses wherever the cathode contraction beats the local anode expansion rate.
